Anita Patel: Quick architecture question — how should we carry attribution across large requests that get chunked and fan-out to multiple model shards? billing needs a single charge, audits need per-chunk provenance. Thoughts?
Matt Cho: Do we actually need per-token provenance for audits, or is per-request + offsets enough?
Cheng Wu: For fraud/abuse and debugability, per-token attribution (or at least per-prefix) is ideal. But that balloons event size.
Katie Ramirez: tradeoff: small events (one per original request) are cheap for billing but useless for detailed replay. Large events (per-chunk tokens with provenance) hit storage and throughput.
Anita Patel: Right. I'm thinking a hybrid: emit compact billing events at request granularity, emit optional enriched provenance events that can be sampled or enabled per-customer for audits/backfills.
Matt Cho: Hybrid seems reasonable. We should define a stable correlation key so enriched events can be stitched to the billing event deterministically. e.g., request_id + chunk_index + digest.
Cheng Wu: Agree. Proposal: always emit billing_event {request_id, model, token_count, cost_estimate}. Then async emit provenance_event(s) that reference request_id and include minimal token-level metadata when needed.
Katie Ramirez: What about dedup/backfill complexity? If infra retries a chunk we could get duplicate provenance events. We need idempotency keys and finalization markers.
Anita Patel: Good call. We can use an append-only provenance stream keyed by (request_id, chunk_id, seq). When the router finishes a request, emit a finalization event: provenance_finalized {request_id, total_chunks, checksum}. That lets downstream reconcile.
Matt Cho: For storage sizing: worst-case per-token line would kill us. So provenance_event should use a compressed token run format. Example:  
```
provenance_event: {
  "request_id": "r_abc123",
  "chunk_id": 0,
  "runs": [ {"text": "Hello world", "start_token": 0, "end_token": 2, "attribution": "user_prompt"}, ... ]
}
```
Cheng Wu: Also useful: include a light-weight fingerprint (sha1 or murmur) of the full generated sequence to allow quick mismatch detection during audits without materializing the whole text.
Katie Ramirez: Streaming considerations: some customers use low-latency streaming and need near-real-time billing visibility. Billing events must be generated early (best-effort), but marked provisional until finalization.
Anita Patel: So billing_event has a status: provisional | finalized. Provisional emitted at chunk commit; finalized after provenance_finalized. Charge accountant can operate on finalized only.
ops-bot: Note: deploy v3.14 rolled to canary — meter-producer now includes request_id in all child records :rocket:
Matt Cho: Operationally we need retention tiers: short raw provenance (7-30d), long aggregated audit logs (1-3y) for compliance. That reduces hot storage burden.
Cheng Wu: For compatibility with downstream billing systems, we'll publish a 1.0 event contract: 1) billing_event (compact), 2) provenance_event (optional, sampled), 3) provenance_finalized. Keep fields stable; version via header `schema_version`.
Katie Ramirez: Edge case: multi-model routing (fallbacks). Which model gets charged? Propose charge primary model actually served the token. If fallback occurs mid-request, billing_event should include per-chunk model attribution.
Anita Patel: Agreed. billing_event should allow an array per-chunk: [{chunk_id, model, token_count, cost}]. That keeps single billing record but granular charge.
Matt Cho: Action items: 1) Cheng to draft event schemas and size estimates. 2) Katie to propose retention tiers + cost model. 3) Anita to write RFC follow-up clarifying finalization semantics.
Cheng Wu: I'll throw a quick proto into the repo today. Will include examples for a sampled provenance payload and the compact billing record.
Katie Ramirez: I'll run numbers on storage for different sampling rates (0.1%, 1%, 10%) and share by EOD Thu.
Anita Patel: Thanks — can we aim to freeze the contract by next Tue so eng infra can start the producer changes? :thumbsup:
Matt Cho: SGTM.
